original_question: Morozov constructed a Π-group that is not isomorphic to a subgroup of S_rec. Can one construct such a group so that it is also residually finite, even though it cannot be effectively residually finite?
correct_elements: The draft correctly targets the narrow Morozov/S_rec question from the paper rather than the broader neighboring Problem 15(b). It keeps the essential ingredients: Morozov’s example, the Π-group hypothesis, the obstruction of not being isomorphic to a subgroup of S_rec, the added demand of residual finiteness, and the paper’s accompanying remark that such an example would not be effectively residually finite.
missing_details: In the paper’s local context, a Π-group is a finitely generated group with Π^0_1 word problem; the finite-generation assumption is implicit in the draft but should be stated.
The surrounding setup writes such groups as L = F_k/N, with F_k a finitely generated free group and N the normal subgroup of relators; this ambient presentation is implicit in the draft.
S_rec is left undefined in the draft; to make the question stand-alone, one should identify it as the group of computable (recursive) permutations of ℕ.

The paper gives a specific algorithmic meaning of ‘effectively residually finite’: given a word w in F_k with w not in N, one must compute a finite group Q and a homomorphism r:F_k→Q such that r(N)={e} and r(w)≠e.
The official target is the narrower Problem 15(c), not the broader Problem 15(b) asking for any finitely generated residually finite Π-group that is not effectively residually finite.
The clause ‘it can’t be e.r.f.’ is a consequence/comment recorded by the paper, not an extra hypothesis of the problem.
refined_question: Does there exist a finitely generated residually finite group L = F_k/N whose word problem is Π^0_1 and which is not isomorphic to any subgroup of S_rec, the group of computable permutations of ℕ—that is, can Morozov’s 2000 example of a Π-group not isomorphic to a subgroup of S_rec be made residually finite? The paper notes that any such example would necessarily not be effectively residually finite, meaning that there is no algorithm which, given w ∈ F_k with w ∉ N, computes a finite group Q and a homomorphism r:F_k→Q such that r(N)={e} and r(w)≠e.
justification: The draft is aimed almost verbatim at Problem 15(c) in Andre Nies’s ‘Profinite groups’ subsection. The immediately preceding context on the same page supplies the paper’s exact meanings of ‘effectively residually finite’ and ‘Π-group’ via the definition before Theorem 14 and Theorem 14(a). Problem 15(b) is the broader neighboring existence question about finitely generated residually finite Π-groups that are not effectively residually finite, whereas Problem 15(c) is specifically the Morozov/S_rec version. So the refined question should stay with the narrower S_rec formulation and only incorporate the paper’s own note that any positive answer would yield a non-e.r.f. example.
